pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK; test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
src/index.js item(); 'AC-2' test asserts exact labelled list.
Parameterised filtered query ORDER BY id; 'AC-3' test covers high, low and normal.
'AC-4' test asserts all items in id order with no filter.
'AC-5' test asserts exact nav markup for all four views.
'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__.
'AC-7' test checks exact messages for high, low, normal, and 'No items yet.' in all views on an empty table.

findings.what: The last commit ('Follow-up edits', by a bot) loosened the 'No match' state test from toBe("No low-priority items.") to toBeDefined(). message() returns null when absent, and null is defined, so the assertion can never fail. The spec gives no justification. The AC-7 test still covers the exact text, but the state-table row's own test now proves nothing about the message.
The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the final commit loosened the No match state test. The body also omits that test/traffic.test.js was changed.
findings.fix: Restore the assertion and keep the claim, or state the loosening. Mention the traffic.test.js change.

findings.what: The README describes the filter but not the high/low labels or the 400 on an invalid value.
findings.fix: Add one line on the labels and the 400 response.

findings.what: The 'Empty table' state test checks only the unfiltered view. The AC-7 test covers the filtered views.
findings.fix: Optional: loop over the filter views in the state test.

lenses.note: Spec present with an owner go dated 2026-10-12. The change matches it, and I found no scope added beyond the ask apart from the traffic-check regex change, which AC-8 needs.
All 8 items are implemented and named by tests. The State table rows are each tested, but the No match row's test was weakened in the last commit. The spec file was not edited after the go.
The final commit weakened a test to an assertion that can never fail. I could not run npm test because vitest is not installed in this copy.
README is partly updated; it omits the labels and the 400.
The query is parameterised and the value is validated against a Set. An empty priority value correctly returns 400.
Output is escaped, SQL is bound, and I found no instructions planted in the repo content.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework or style files. The UI is checked through the AC-5 nav test.
No browser or preview is available, and the PR says none.
The title is within 72 characters. The 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' claim is false because of the last commit.
